standards_review.notes: 4 subjects in 4779872aa9..HEAD match the EPMCDME-####: Description format (ticket EPMCDME-15392, capitalised description).
Headers, typing and modern unions met. Unmet: none of the 3 new modules has 'from __future__ import annotations' as code-quality.md asks. Ruff and license-check not run.

Guide checks met: local logout keeps Depends(authenticate); GET resolver fails closed and logs class names only. Concern: cross-site GET /v1/user/log_out can now trigger TMS deletion; SameSite unverified.

findings.title: Unbounded TMS delete can stall logout
findings.problem: Both logout routes await asyncio.to_thread(remove_user_tokens_on_logout, ...) with no timeout (local_auth_router.py:241, user.py:159), and the new user resolution at user.py:145 has none either. The 'never raises' contract bounds exceptions, not latency.
findings.impact: GET /user/log_out used to be credential- and DB-free and always completed. A stalled Postgres, Redis or TMS call now hangs the logout response and pins a default-executor thread shared with other to_thread users. Reachability of a stall was unconfirmed: no DB or socket timeout outside the diff was read.
findings.recommendation: Bound the cleanup (and the GET resolution) with asyncio.wait_for and a configured timeout, treating expiry as a sanitized warning followed by the normal logout. wait_for does not stop the worker thread, so also ensure the TMS delete path has a statement or socket timeout.

findings.title: Header-less logout navigation may skip purge
findings.problem: codemie-ui logs out with a top-level navigation to /v1/user/log_out (codemie-ui auth.ts:94), which cannot carry an Authorization header. With JWKS_VALIDATION_ENABLED, JwksValidatingIdp.authenticate requires a Bearer header (jwks_validating.py:124-130) and raises 401; _resolve_logout_user_id swallows it and skips cleanup with a warning. Every GET test mocks get_idp_provider and get_user_provider, so none drives the real IdP chain or a cookie-only request.
findings.impact: For Keycloak deployments in this mode the ticket's core behavior (TMS tokens removed on logout) may never run, and the passing tests cannot show it. Reachability unconfirmed: an authenticating proxy may inject the header, and the inner enterprise IdP was not readable.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that sends GET /v1/user/log_out with only the session cookie through the real IdpFactory (JWKS on and off) and asserts cleanup runs with the cookie user's id, or explicitly asserts it is skipped. If skipped in JWKS mode, resolve the identity from the session credential using the same validation.

findings.title: Cross-site GET can trigger TMS token deletion
findings.problem: GET /v1/user/log_out, resolved from the session credential alone with no CSRF token, Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check, now also deletes every stored MCP and tool OAuth token of that user. Before this change the same request only cleared the session cookie. A cross-site top-level GET carries SameSite=Lax cookies, and cookie attributes are not set in this repo.
findings.impact: A third-party page can force a victim's browser to this URL and destroy persisted third-party credentials, forcing re-authorization of every MCP server and tool OAuth grant. Reachability unconfirmed and tied to CR-002: if header-less requests never resolve a user, the purge does not run and the exposure is absent.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether cross-site-initiated logout (e.g. IdP-initiated links) should purge tokens. The UI is out of scope and cannot switch to POST, so the likely option is to run the purge only for same-origin or same-site requests (Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin/Referer) while still deleting the cookie and redirecting.

findings.title: New modules omit __future__ annotations import
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports) says to add 'from __future__ import annotations' in new modules. logout_token_cleanup.py, tests/codemie/service/security/test_logout_token_cleanup.py and test_logout_token_cleanup_mock_tms.py all omit it.
findings.impact: The documented code-quality convention for new modules is not followed, so the standards check is only partially met.
findings.recommendation: Add 'from __future__ import annotations' after the license header and module docstring in each of the three new files.

findings.title: Cache purges not isolated or synchronized
findings.problem: _purge_process_caches runs token_exchange_service.purge_user_cache then oidc_token_exchange_service.purge_user_cache with no per-step isolation, so if the first raises the OIDC cache and its store.purge_fallback_for_user are skipped. Because the purge sits in a finally, its exception also replaces the delete's exception and the failed TMS delete goes unlogged. The purges now run on a worker thread and iterate shared TTLCache and _fallback dicts (oidc_token_exchange_service.py:345, tms_token_store.py:195) with no lock seen around them, so a concurrent insert or eviction can raise 'changed size during iteration'.
findings.impact: Cached user tokens can survive logout after only a one-line warning, and the TMS delete failure can be hidden. Concurrency reachability was unconfirmed; the same list-then-pop pattern already exists in invalidate_all_for_user.
findings.recommendation: Run the delete and each purge under its own try/except that logs the class name, so one failure neither skips another purge nor masks the delete failure. Snapshot the keys safely (a lock shared with get/put, or retry on RuntimeError) in both purge_fallback_for_user and OIDCTokenExchangeService.purge_user_cache.
